name: tera_render
description:
Render a Tera template, optionally with a JSON context. Supports the full Tera vocabulary: variables, filters, conditionals, for loops, autoescape, and inclusion. Options are keyword-only named parameters with defaults — `autoescape := false` for non-HTML output, `template_path := './templates/*.html'` to load templates from disk by name. They must be constant expressions; unknown option names or values of the wrong type are rejected when the query is bound, and a NULL argument (including a NULL option) makes the result NULL.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** Tera's `get_env()` function is disabled (it would expose the server's environment variables) unless you `SET tera_allow_get_env = true` while `enable_external_access` is on. `template_path` files are read through DuckDB's file system, so they are refused when `enable_external_access` is false unless `allowed_directories`/`allowed_paths` cover them. The context must be a JSON object (any value that casts to JSON works, including a struct or a whole row). Templates that would overflow the stack — self-including or self-importing templates, recursive macros, or more than 64 levels of nested tags or brackets — are rejected with an error.

examples.code: SELECT tera_render('{{ user.name }} has {{ tags | length }} tags', {'user': {'name': 'Alice'}, 'tags': ['a', 'b']});

-- browser-unavailable: File-based templates are unavailable in this browser build. Run this example in native DuckDB with your template files.
SELECT tera_render('email.html', '{"name":"Alice"}', template_path := './templates/*.html');

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Template source, or a template name when `template_path` is set.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Context the template is rendered against: a JSON object — a literal, a JSON column, `json_object(...)` built from columns, or any value that casts to JSON such as a struct or a whole row. Arrays, scalars and JSON `null` are rejected on the DuckDB 2.0 build. Omit it for templates without variables.

parameters.name: autoescape
parameters.description: HTML-escape interpolated values (`B&O` becomes `B&O`), in inline templates and in `template_path` files whatever their extension. Pass `false` for plain text, configs, SQL or JSON output.

parameters.name: template_path
parameters.description: A template file, or a glob of them (for example `'./templates/*.html'` or `'./templates/**/*.html'`); templates are named by their path relative to the glob's directory. When set, `template` is a template name, which enables `{% extends %}` / `{% include %}` / `{% import %}`. Empty means inline templates only. On the DuckDB 2.0 build the files are read once per query through DuckDB's file system, so `enable_external_access`, `allowed_directories` and `allowed_paths` apply, and a glob that matches nothing is an error.

parameters.name: autoescape_extensions
parameters.description: Only used with `template_path`: when non-empty, file templates are HTML-escaped only if their name ends with one of these suffixes (for example `['.html']`). With the default `[]`, `autoescape` applies to every template. Has no effect when `autoescape` is false. Inline templates follow `autoescape` and ignore this list. Must not contain NULL elements.
